title: Rollout ops quick-capture — surge scenario rehearsal
content:
Purpose: quick capture of today’s 30m rehearsal focusing on panel UI + analytics during an artificial surge. Goal: validate canary gating and telemetry flows so we can confidently flip the new feature flag next week (sprint 42).

Attendees:
- Priya (owner)
- Jonas (frontend)
- Maya (telemetry / analytics)
- Ethan (rollout tooling / flags)
- Samira (on-call SRE join)

Summary of rehearsal steps performed:
1) Start small canary (5% traffic) for panel-v2 via rollout service (CONSOLE-842).
2) Injected synthetic surge (~3x baseline RPS) from test harness for 10 minutes (source: surge-harness-2027-03-08).
3) Observed client-side errors, telemetry funnel, and slow P50 on initial hits due to cold renders and missing KV cache priming.
4) Scaled canary to 20% for 5 minutes; validated fallback behavior and automatic rollback threshold (error_rate > 2% for 3m).

Key observations / findings:
- UI: initial cold-start caused ~250ms additional render latency on first N requests; remediation: pre-warm client bundle cache via CDN invalidation window shrink and add edge prefetch (Jonas). Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5173.
- Analytics: missing event for `panel.rendered` in 12% of sessions during surge due to batching backpressure; this skews rollouts by under-reporting success. Maya to add a low-latency flush path for critical events.
- Rollout tooling: the automatic rollback trigger fired correctly in the test harness when error_rate crossed 2.5%, but we noted a 30s detection lag because metric aggregation window is 60s. Proposed change: reduce detection window to 30s for feature flags in canary mode (Ethan).
- SRE: backend CPU spikes correlated with un-primed KV lookups under burst; Samira recommends a short-lived warming job post-deploy to populate caches and an autoscale tweak.

Decisions made:
- Keep feature flag in 10% canary overnight, but gate further expansion behind two conditions: (1) `panel.rendered` event rate >= 96% and (2) P50 render latency delta < 150ms vs baseline.
- Implement urgent telemetry patch (low-latency flush) and a frontend pre-warm task. Both must be merged and smoke-tested before tomorrow EOD.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Jonas: open follow-up PR to add CDN prefetch + small bundle split to reduce cold render (PR draft by EOD 2027-03-09).
- Maya: instrument critical event flush path and add test simulation to surge harness (tests + metrics by 2027-03-10). Linked to CONSOLE-842.
- Ethan: change flag detection window to 30s for canaries and add a jitter limiter to avoid flapping (deploy config by 2027-03-11).
- Samira: create short-lived cache-warm job in infra repo and propose autoscale tweak (ops ticket by 2027-03-10).
- Priya: run sign-off checklist and coordinate a quick stakeholder demo if all items land (blocker check-in 2027-03-11 10:00 PT).

Risks / open questions:
- If the telemetry flush adds noticeable client bandwidth, product is concerned about mobile users on metered networks. Need quantification; Maya to include simulated payload delta.
- Are we comfortable with a 30s detection window for all canaries? Might increase noise for very spiky apps. Consider flag-level override config.
- Post-rollback behavior: ensure session affinity doesn’t keep clients pinned to bad variant. Engineering to validate sticky-session behavior under rollout.

Metrics captured during rehearsal (baseline vs canary surge):
- Baseline P50 render: 180ms -> Canary initial cold: 430ms (delta +250ms)
- Baseline panel.rendered event rate: 99% -> Canary surge: 87%
- Error rate baseline: 0.4% -> Canary surge peak: 2.8% (triggered rollback in harness)

Follow-ups / suggested experiments:
- Run a prioritized set of 1000 warm-start requests immediately post-deploy to pre-populate edge and KV caches (experiment: warm-job-v1).
- Add a single-field lightweight `panel.boot` event emitted as early as possible so we have a faster signal for renders.

Notes / references:
- Ticket: CONSOLE-842 (rollout gating tweaks)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5173 (frontend bundle prefetch draft)
- Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/Rollout+Rehearsals
- Slack log summary: #console-rollouts thread 2027-03-08 (search "surge rehearsal")

Quick retrospective: the rehearsal validated the rollback plumbing end-to-end — good signal fidelity once telemetry was flowing. Biggest gaps are cache-priming and critical-event delivery under client-side batching. If we close the three action items this week, confident to expand to 50% next Tuesday.
